codes.B: Any source, but the molecule must occur in cannabis
codes.C: Natural only, synthetic terpenes or flavors banned
codes.D: Flavor or sensory ban (must taste like cannabis, or a banned flavor list)
codes.G: Disclosure and dossier: label listing, supplier COA, CAS, grade

dates: Colorado expanded residual solvent panel enforced
UK flavour and descriptor consultation closes
Italy Constitutional Court hearing on hemp flower ban
US: synthesized and converted cannabinoids lose hemp status
US: total THC hemp rules for naturally occurring cannabinoids
EU cosmetics allergen labeling applies to all products

c:840.name: United States (federal)
vape: No federal terpene rule; hemp THC rules tighten
preroll: Hemp THCA pre-rolls lose status Dec 11, 2026
c:840.summary: No federal rule restricts terpenes in cannabis products; states govern. The federal risk is the hemp market shrinking.
c:840.source: FDA says GRAS status does not cover inhalation, and FEMA does not evaluate flavors for vaping. Keep GRAS claims to edibles and beverages.
c:840.additives: No federal ban on vitamin E acetate, MCT or PEG; guidance only after EVALI.
c:840.disclosure: USPS PACT Act rule bans mailing hemp and cannabis vapes to consumers; B2B needs Form 4615E.
c:840.watch: Converted cannabinoids out Nov 12, 2026; total THC 0.4 mg per container from Dec 11, 2026 (H.R. 6500). Medical marijuana in Schedule III since Apr 23, 2026.

us:06.name: California
vape: Botanical OK if natural and cannabis-like
us:06.summary: Inhalables may contain only cannabis, terpenes or FDA inactive ingredients approved for inhalation (4 CCR 17303.1).
us:06.source: Botanical terpenes allowed if naturally occurring and found in cannabis. Synthetic terpenes banned. Natural flavors that do not add to cannabis aroma banned: menthol, mint, mango, strawberry, grape, orange, clove, cinnamon, vanilla, coconut, cherry, coffee, chocolate and more.
us:06.additives: Nothing that raises potency, toxicity or addictiveness (17300).
us:06.disclosure: All ingredients on label. Edibles: GRAS or FDA-permitted ingredients (17301).
sources: DCC guidance: New requirements for inhaled cannabis products (PDF)
4 CCR § 17303.1 Additional requirements for inhaled products

us:08.name: Colorado
us:08.summary: Botanical terpenes are allowed. The live issue is the expanded residual solvent panel, enforced from Sept 28, 2026.
us:08.source: "Botanically Derived Compounds and/or terpenoids" permitted (3-335(I)). Additives that make products addictive, child-appealing or misleading banned (3-335(J)).
us:08.additives: PEG, vitamin E acetate and MCT banned in inhalables (3-335(K)); DMSO banned in production.
us:08.disclosure: Vapes and concentrates list all ingredients (3-1010). Inhaled heavy metals: Pb 0.5, As 0.2, Cd 0.2, Hg 0.1 ppm.
us:08.watch: Expanded residual-solvent panel (Table 4-215(J)(6)(a)1), enforced from Sept 28, 2026: 31 solvents, 18 of them new and non-detect, including butyl acetate, isobutyl acetate and 3-methyl-1-butanol (isoamyl alcohol), which are common flavour esters and alcohols. Applies to solvent-based concentrates, not pre-rolls. Permanent rules effective Nov 1, 2026.
sources: SC Labs: updated RSA testing for Colorado

us:53.name: Washington
preroll: Flower cannot be treated to alter smell
us:53.summary: Botanical terpenes that occur in cannabis are allowed regardless of source; synthetic terpenes are excluded.
us:53.source: Defines botanical terpenes, synthetic terpenes and characterizing flavor (WAC 314-55-010). No characterizing flavor ban in the 2021 rule.
us:53.disclosure: All additives and terpenes listed on concentrate labels (314-55-105, -1055).
us:53.watch: Preproposal rulemakings on heavy metals and COA expiry.

us:41.name: Oregon
us:41.summary: Botanical terpenes are allowed but Oregon has the strictest supplier documentation.
us:41.source: Non-cannabis additive = anything not from marijuana or hemp, including essential oils and isolates (845-025-1015). No flavor ban found.
us:41.additives: Squalene, squalane, vitamin E acetate, MCT and other triglycerides, PG (845-025-3265).
us:41.disclosure: Supplier ingredient list: CAS with isomer, % ranges within 20 points, statement of intended inhalation use. Label identity says "non-cannabis additive"; OLCC label pre-approval.

us:32.name: Nevada
us:32.summary: Cannabis-derived terpenes allowed; botanical terpenes need CCB approval; any synthetic means denial.
us:32.source: CCB Terpene Guidance (2026). Terpenes capped at 10% of the final inhalable.
us:32.additives: Vitamin E acetate, PEG, DMSO, MCT, phytol.
us:32.disclosure: Full COA (solvents, metals, pesticides); summary COAs rejected. Supplier confirms no acetone, toluene or methanol. Top 3 terpenes on label.

us:35.name: New Mexico
us:35.summary: No terpene source or flavor rule; standard banned-additive list.
us:35.additives: PEG, polypropylene glycol, vitamin E acetate, MCT (16.8.2.29).
us:35.disclosure: Ingredients and sub-ingredients listed; SDS on site.

us:04.name: Arizona
us:04.summary: No rule on terpenes, flavors or inhalable additives found.
us:04.disclosure: Ingredients in order of abundance (R9-18-310); solvents and metals testing.

us:30.name: Montana
us:30.watch: HB 636 dose limits and HB 792 warnings from Jul 1, 2026.

us:02.name: Alaska
us:02.summary: No source rule, but products are approved one by one.
us:02.source: None specific. A 2025 vape with citrus essential oil drew a $63k fine.

us:49.name: Utah (medical)
vape: No source rule; no candy flavors
us:49.summary: Flavor names allowed if not candy-like; GMP under 21 CFR 111.
us:49.disclosure: Any named terpene must be lab-verified; all ingredients and allergens listed; food grade.

us:36.name: New York
us:36.summary: Botanical terpenes allowed, synthetic banned; overall taste must be indistinguishable from cannabis.
us:36.source: Banned: menthol, mint, cotton candy, bubble gum, candy, clove, vanilla, chocolate, ice cream, soda, cereal, dessert, concept flavors (9 NYCRR 123.6(f)(9)).
us:36.additives: PEG, vitamin E acetate, MCT, benzoic acid, diketones, artificial coloring. Terpenes capped at 10%.
us:36.disclosure: Licensee keeps full source information on every botanical terpene; all other ingredients pharma grade.
us:36.watch: New packaging and labeling rules; compliance deadline Jun 3, 2026.

us:25.name: Massachusetts
us:25.summary: Botanical terpenes allowed; label must say they come from sources other than cannabis.
us:25.source: "This product was produced using terpenes derived from sources other than cannabis" (935 CMR 500.105(5)(c)7).
us:25.additives: Not found in the sections reviewed.
us:25.disclosure: Each additive's amount and % of volume on label; COA kept for every thickener, thinner or terpene (500.130).

us:34.name: New Jersey
us:34.summary: Every ingredient must carry a compendial grade; botanical terpenes are not banned by name.
us:34.source: USP-NF, AR, ACS or FCC grade (N.J.A.C. 17:30-11.6(d)). Artificial flavorings known to be harmful banned.
us:34.additives: PEG, PG, VG, vitamin E acetate, acetic acid, FDA harmful tobacco constituents. Terpenes capped at 10%.
us:34.disclosure: Excipients and major terpenoids on label.

us:09.name: Connecticut
us:09.summary: Terpenes and additives must come from CT cannabis or USDA-plan hemp via a credentialed processor.
us:09.source: Regs. Conn. State Agencies 21a-421j-26. Terpenes capped at 10%.
us:09.additives: PEG, vitamin E acetate, MCT, squalene, squalane (21a-421j-27, 2022 text).
us:09.disclosure: Hemp-derived terpenes are the only route in.

us:44.name: Rhode Island
vape: Flavors solely from cannabis or hemp
us:44.summary: Inhalable concentrates may carry only flavors derived solely from cannabis and/or hemp (560-RICR-10-10-2, 2.4.3).
us:44.disclosure: Vape consumer testing certificate; device temperature controls.

us:50.name: Vermont
vape: Flavored vapes banned; cannabis-identical terpenes allowed
preroll: No characterizing flavor not in cannabis
us:50.summary: Flavored oil vape products are banned (7 V.S.A. 868). Added terpenes must occur naturally in cannabis.
us:50.source: Strain-mimicking blends of cannabis terpenes arguably allowed; flavor profiles are not.
us:50.additives: CCB approved-ingredient schedule; terpenes capped at 10%; disposables banned.

us:10.name: Delaware
us:10.summary: Any diluent must be "100% naturally occurring plant-derived terpene oil" (4 Del. Admin. Code 5001-8.1.5).
us:10.source: Natural botanical terpenes fit; synthetic or nature-identical do not.
us:10.additives: MCT, PEG, PG, VG, vitamin E acetate, diacetyl, squalene.
us:10.disclosure: Edibles cannot look like candy or fruit.

us:27.name: Minnesota
us:27.summary: Vapes take natural plant-derived terpenes; infused flower may only use cannabis-derived products.
us:27.source: No artificial or synthetic compounds; other inactives must be on FDA IID (9810.2205). Pre-rolls: 9810.2203.
us:27.additives: MCT, PEG, VG, vitamin E acetate, diacetyl, squalene.
us:27.disclosure: Added terpenes tested to within 15% of label.

us:26.name: Michigan
us:26.summary: Botanical terpenes chemically identical to cannabis terpenes are exempt from the FDA-approval rule for inactives.
us:26.source: Other inactive ingredients need FDA IID approval for inhalation (R 420.206, 420.403).
us:26.additives: Vitamin E acetate and 4 MCTs tested in every cartridge since Oct 1, 2024.
us:26.disclosure: Inactives listed on label. May 2025 enforcement over MCT in vapes.

us:42.name: Pennsylvania (medical)
vape: Per-product DOH approval; injunction in force
us:42.summary: Every added substance needs DOH approval. Since Mar 17, 2026 the FDA inhalation test for botanical terpenes is enjoined.
us:42.source: AES Compassionate Care v. Bogen, No. 176 MD 2025. About 650 vapes recalled in 2022.
us:42.additives: Diacetyl and 2,3-pentanedione weighed as hazards; excipients pharma grade (28 Pa. Code 1151a.27).

us:24.name: Maryland
us:24.summary: Botanical terpenes appear allowed if disclosed.
us:24.disclosure: Each terpene by weight and all non-cannabis ingredients on label (COMAR 14.17.18.03).

us:29.name: Missouri
us:29.summary: Labels cannot group "natural flavors" or "botanically derived terpenes"; each ingredient listed.
us:29.source: No source ban (19 CSR 100-1.120). Ingestibles have a grouping variance; inhalables do not.
us:29.additives: Vitamin E acetate limited to 5 ppm.
us:29.disclosure: Full terpene breakdown exposes formulas on the label.

us:17.name: Illinois
us:17.summary: Botanical terpenes appear allowed with disclosure.
us:17.additives: Vitamin E "in any form" (8 Ill. Adm. Code 1300.475).

us:51.name: Virginia
us:51.summary: Only vitamin E acetate and potency-raising additives are banned.
us:51.additives: Vitamin E acetate (3VAC10-50-50(H)); alcohol, caffeine, nicotine.

us:39.name: Ohio
us:39.summary: Ingredient and vendor records per lot; additive rules not found.
us:39.watch: Rules Package 7 (proposed): top 3 terpenes on label, 10 terpenes tested.

us:12.name: Florida (medical)
us:12.summary: No color additives; nothing attractive to children (F.S. 381.986).
us:12.watch: New edibles, labeling and extraction rules effective Aug 24, 2026.

us:15.name: Hawaii (medical)
us:15.summary: Vape devices restricted to cannabis-derived extracts; "no allowance for any other additives".

us:23.name: Maine
us:23.summary: No terpene or flavor rules in the adult-use Chapter 1 rule; manufacturing rule not accessible.

us:05.name: Arkansas (medical)
us:05.summary: Only a general ban on additives that raise potency or toxicity.

us:40.name: Oklahoma (medical)
us:40.summary: No vape additive or terpene rules found in OAC 442:10.

us:22.name: Louisiana (medical)
us:22.summary: July 2025 emergency rule lists inhalers and flower; no additive rules.

c:124.name: Canada (federal)
vape: Flavouring agents OK; Schedule B grade
preroll: Nothing on dried cannabis; an infused pre-roll becomes an extract
c:124.summary: Natural terpene blends allowed in extracts as flavouring agents; promotion limited to cannabis flavour.
c:124.source: Extracts may contain only carriers, flavouring agents and stability substances (SOR/2018-144 s. 101.3(1)). No sweeteners. No promotion of TVPA Schedule 3 flavours other than cannabis (s. 104.12).
c:124.additives: TVPA Schedule 2 substances, sugars and sweeteners, colourants. Ethanol up to 10 mg per activation (2025).
c:124.disclosure: Each inhaled-extract ingredient needs a Schedule B standard (USP, FCC). 60-day new product notice.
c:124.watch: 2021 proposal to limit flavouring agents to cannabis-identical substances is dormant.

ca:QC.name: Quebec
vape: Cannabis flavour only; SQDC takes cannabis-derived terpenes
preroll: Extract rules apply: cannabis flavour only
ca:QC.summary: "Cannabis extract may not contain any characteristic flavour or odour other than those of cannabis" (CQLR c. C-5.3, r. 0.1, s. 6).
ca:QC.source: The regulation is a sensory test. SQDC buying practice accepts only cannabis-derived terpenes (trade press, not regulation). No colourants.
ca:QC.additives: No THC-strengthening components; THC capped at 30%.
ca:QC.disclosure: SQDC product specifications (not yet obtained in writing).

ca:NS.name: Nova Scotia
vape: Natural only; must read as cannabis
ca:NS.summary: No characterizing scent or flavour other than cannabis, and no synthetic flavouring agent (N.S. Reg. 72/2025, s. 8).
ca:NS.source: Eybna's natural positioning fits if the blend reads as cannabis.

ca:NL.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
ca:NL.summary: Vapes allowed since late 2022; NLC accepts no flavours except natural flavours and terpenes related to cannabis.

ca:PE.name: Prince Edward Island
ca:PE.summary: Bill 71 (2024) confirms the vape flavour ban does not apply to cannabis.

ca:NB.name: New Brunswick
vape: E-cig flavour ban may reach cannabis
ca:NB.summary: E-cigarette flavour ban since Sept 1, 2021; application to cannabis vapes unverified.

c:276.name: Germany
vape: Medical extracts by prescription; hemp/CBD liquids under tobacco law
preroll: Club flower must be additive-free (KCanG 21(1)); medical flower is monograph-grade
c:276.summary: Open medical market (MedCanG): pharmacies dispense flower, extracts, distillates and THC vape cartridges on prescription, some with added terpenes. Recreational is legal for home grow and non-profit clubs (KCanG), but clubs may only pass on flower and resin with no additives. Nicotine-free and CBD vape liquids fall under the Tabakerzeugnisgesetz.
c:276.source: Medical: terpenes allowed as declared ingredients within the GMP/pharmacy dossier. Hemp vapes: food-grade flavors allowed, subject to TabakerzG ingredient rules. No source (cannabis-derived) requirement found.
c:276.additives: KCanG 21(1): no tobacco, nicotine, food or other additives in club cannabis. TabakerzG bans VEA, diacetyl, acetoin, pentanedione, caffeine, taurine and CMR substances in liquids.
c:276.disclosure: Medical: GMP, pharmacy release testing, full composition. Vape liquids: full ingredient list, TPD2 notification.
c:276.watch: MedCanG amendment (mail-order flower ban); EU single-use vape ban and TPD revision. Draft 5th TabakerzV amendment (Jan 2026) would ban menthol, 1,8-cineole (eucalyptol), isopulegol, menthone, menthyl acetate, synthetic cooling agents and sucralose in e-cigarettes and refills, six months after publication.
sources: BMLEH draft: 5th amendment to TabakerzV (23 Jan 2026)

c:756.name: Switzerland
vape: Pilot products with additives need approval
preroll: Hemp under 1% THC is a tobacco substitute
c:756.summary: BetmPV pilot trials may include products mixed with additives, with approval; framework expires May 14, 2031.
c:756.disclosure: TabPG for hemp smoking products since Oct 1, 2024.

c:528.name: Netherlands
vape: No cannabis vapes; e-liquids limited to tobacco flavours
preroll: Grower pre-packed only; terpene rule not verified
c:528.summary: The closed coffeeshop chain allows flower, hash, pre-rolls and edibles; concentrates banned; no vapes.
c:528.ecig: Since 1 Jan 2024 e-liquids, with or without nicotine, may only be tobacco-flavoured or unflavoured, using a positive list of 16 flavouring substances. Common terpenes and plant extracts are not on the list, so terpene blends cannot be used in e-liquids here.

c:470.name: Malta
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed under EU TPD rules
preroll: Dried flowers only; no pre-roll channel
c:470.summary: Associations may distribute dried cannabis flowers only.
c:470.additives: All other forms prohibited without ARUC consent.
c:470.ecig: Malta has no flavour restrictions on e-liquids, which follow the EU Tobacco Products Directive (2016 regulations, Cap. 315): 20 mg/ml nicotine cap, high-purity non-CMR ingredients, and notification to the Superintendent of Public Health before sale. Cross-border distance sales are banned.

c:442.name: Luxembourg
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed under EU TPD rules
c:442.ecig: Flavoured e-liquids are legal under the EU Tobacco Products Directive as transposed in the anti-tobacco law of 2006. The 2025 reform banned flavours in heated tobacco and nicotine pouches, not e-liquids. Ingredients must be high purity, non-CMR and safe heated or unheated, and products are notified via EU-CEG before sale.

c:203.name: Czech Republic
vape: Low-THC extracts licensed; no flavor rule found
c:203.summary: Psychomodulatory substances law (Jul 1, 2025) licenses low-THC (1% or less) extracts and kratom.

c:250.name: France
vape: CBD e-liquids unaffected by food sweep
c:250.summary: CBD flower allowed; HHC and analogues banned; CBD foods being removed from May 15, 2026.

c:380.name: Italy
preroll: Hemp flower banned; no terpene-specific rule
c:380.summary: DL 48/2025 Art. 18 bans hemp inflorescences; oral CBD ban referred to CJEU.
c:380.watch: Constitutional Court hearing around Oct 20 to 21, 2026.

c:724.name: Spain
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed today; tobacco-only decree pending
preroll: No smokable route; no terpene-specific rule
c:724.summary: RD 903/2025: standardised extracts for magistral formulas dispensed by hospital pharmacies.
sources: Ministerio de Sanidad: draft RD amending RD 579/2017
c:724.ecig: Flavoured e-liquids are legal under RD 579/2017 (EU Tobacco Products Directive). A draft royal decree limiting all e-liquids, including nicotine-free, to tobacco flavours has passed EU review and awaits final approval; after publication non-tobacco flavours get about 12 months to sell through. The draft also limits ingredients to high-purity, non-hazardous substances.

c:616.name: Poland
c:616.summary: Nicotine-free e-liquids brought under composition and sales rules (TRIS 2025/0055/PL).
c:616.source: Composition rules apply to non-nicotine vapes.

c:826.name: United Kingdom
vape: Act covers vapes with or without nicotine
c:826.summary: Tobacco and Vapes Act 2026 (Royal Assent Apr 29, 2026) enables flavour, descriptor and packaging limits for non-nicotine vapes.
c:826.disclosure: CBD isolate novel foods provisionally at 10 mg/day.

eu.name: European Union (baseline)
preroll: Herbal smoking products: no flavour ban
eu.summary: EU tobacco flavour rules do not reach nicotine-free vapes or herbal smoking products today; national rules vary.
eu.source: Flavouring Regulation 1334/2008 governs food only: natural flavouring substances, 95/5 rule for natural claims, Annex III caps on pulegone, estragole, methyleugenol, safrole.
eu.additives: CLP: d-limonene and linalool are sensitisers, EUH208/H317 labeling for blends.
eu.disclosure: Cosmetics allergens Reg. 2023/1545: 82 allergens, new products from Jul 31, 2026, all from Jul 31, 2028. CBD foods not yet authorised; EFSA positive opinion Sept 21, 2026 (about 2 mg/day).
eu.watch: TPD revision proposal expected Q4 2026 with stricter flavour rules and wider product scope.

c:376.name: Israel
preroll: Rolled cigarettes standard; additives need approval
c:376.summary: IMC-GMP 152 standard forms: inflorescence, rolled cigarettes, oil extract. Other forms need MoH approval.
c:376.source: Terpenes neither allowed nor banned by name; every non-cannabis component on the label (8.1.2).
c:376.watch: Smoked cannabis phase-out halted May 6, 2026. Procedures 107 and 109 not reviewed.

c:036.name: Australia
c:036.summary: TGO 93 governs quality; cannabis vape devices need ARTG or TGA notification.
c:036.source: TGO 110 flavour limits (mint, menthol, tobacco) likely do not apply to cannabis (unverified).
c:036.watch: TGA review (response Feb 20, 2026) on inhaled extracts and plain packaging.

c:554.name: New Zealand
vape: Excipients need a Ph. Eur. monograph
c:554.summary: No smokable products (reg 19); no excipient without a Ph. Eur. monograph (reg 20).
c:554.source: Most terpene blends fail the monograph test.

c:764.name: Thailand
c:764.summary: Flower prescription-only from Jun 26, 2025; e-cigarettes and e-liquids banned.
c:764.source: Extracts at or under 0.2% THC fall under Thai FDA food and cosmetic rules.

c:392.name: Japan
c:392.summary: THC residue limits since Dec 12, 2024: oils 10 ppm, beverages 0.1 ppm, other products 1 ppm.
c:392.source: Terpene inputs need a THC-free COA at ppm level.

c:410.name: South Korea
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed; nicotine liquids regulated as tobacco since Apr 2026
c:410.summary: CBD remains a narcotic; imported approved drugs only.
sources: Korea Times: synthetic nicotine loophole closed
c:410.ecig: Flavoured e-liquids are legal. Since 24 Apr 2026 nicotine liquids, including synthetic nicotine, are regulated as tobacco: licensed retail, 20 mg/ml cap, 10 ml containers, no online sales, and no flavour names or images on packs. Makers must report harmful-component test results (Tobacco Harmfulness Management Act, Nov 2025). Diketones (diacetyl, 2,3-pentanedione) and vitamin E acetate should be avoided.
c:410.watch: Blends containing hemp-derived CBD are excluded, since CBD is a narcotic in Korea.

c:076.name: Brazil
c:076.summary: RDC 1.015/2026 allows the inhaled route (Art. 7) and bans flower.

c:170.name: Colombia
c:170.summary: Decree 1138 (Oct 27, 2025) authorizes medical flower and magistral preparations; additive rules pending.
c:170.source: Res. 227/2022 allows non-psychoactive derivatives in supplements.

c:484.name: Mexico
vape: Vapes banned with or without nicotine
c:484.summary: Constitutional vape ban since Jan 2025; Dec 2025 Health Law reform covers oils, resins and waxes.

c:032.name: Argentina
c:032.summary: Hemp licensing regime (Res. 69/2026) for medicinal, nutritional and cosmetic uses.

c:858.name: Uruguay
c:858.summary: Medical decree allows flower, extracts, oils and mixtures.

c:710.name: South Africa
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed; flavour powers pending in Parliament
c:710.summary: CBD Schedule 4, THC Schedule 6, low-dose exemptions; hemp defined at 2% THC or less from Dec 1, 2025.
c:710.ecig: Vape liquids, with or without nicotine, have no product-specific law yet and pay an excise of ZAR 2.90/ml. The Tobacco Products and Electronic Delivery Systems Control Bill (B33-2022), still in committee, would let the Health Minister ban non-tobacco flavours and specific ingredients by regulation.

c:504.name: Morocco
vape: Medical & pharmaceutical products only, under ANRAC licence
preroll: Medical product forms set by ANRAC licence; smokable products not confirmed
c:504.summary: Law No. 13.21 legalised cannabis for medical, pharmaceutical and industrial use, including cosmetics. Recreational use remains illegal under national narcotics law. All legal activity is licensed and monitored by ANRAC (National Agency for the Regulation of Cannabis-related Activities).
c:504.source: No terpene-specific rules published; medical and pharmaceutical products are authorised case by case under ANRAC licensing.
c:504.disclosure: Licensed supply chain under ANRAC; product dossier per authorisation.
c:504.watch: Unlicensed cultivation outside the designated legal zones is prosecuted. Cosmetic and industrial uses are also permitted.

c:356.name: India
vape: E-cigarettes banned (PECA 2019); cannabis flower and resin illegal under NDPS Act
preroll: Ganja (flower) and charas (resin) illegal under NDPS Act
c:356.summary: Cannabis is controlled under the NDPS Act, 1985: producing, selling or consuming flower (ganja) and resin (charas) is a federal offence. The Act excludes bhang (leaves and seeds), which states regulate. Ayurvedic 'Vijaya' (cannabis leaf) medicines approved by the Ministry of AYUSH are sold on prescription in oral and topical forms. Hemp cultivation, research and medical work run under state licences, and FSSAI permits hemp seed, seed oil and flour as food.
c:356.source: No cannabis-specific terpene rules. Leaf-based Ayurvedic products follow AYUSH rules; hemp seed foods follow FSSAI standards.
c:356.disclosure: AYUSH product licence for Vijaya medicines; FSSAI standards for hemp seed foods.
c:356.watch: Imported CBD oils are not AYUSH products and have no FSSAI approval; retailers supply them on prescription for personal use. Bhang legality differs by state.
sources: FSSAI: Hemp seeds and seed products

c:688.name: Serbia
vape: E-liquid flavourings: allowed under the Law on Tobacco
c:688.summary: Cannabis is illegal; there is no medical or adult-use cannabis market. E-cigarettes and e-liquids, with or without nicotine, are regulated as related products under the Law on Tobacco.
c:688.disclosure: Tobacco Administration registration for e-liquid producers and importers.
c:688.ecig: Since 1 Jan 2025: 20 mg/ml nicotine cap, 10 ml refills, 2 ml disposables, no online sales, and producer/importer registration with the Tobacco Administration. There is no tobacco-only rule; a draft ban on sweets, candy and chocolate flavours has not been confirmed in the final law.
c:688.watch: Confirm whether confectionery-type flavours (sweets, candy, chocolate) are restricted before launching dessert profiles.

c:578.name: Norway
vape: Nicotine e-cigs banned; nicotine-free tobacco flavour only
c:578.summary: Cannabis is illegal outside prescription medicines. Nicotine e-cigarettes remain banned even after the EU Tobacco Products Directive took effect in Norway on 30 Mar 2026.
c:578.ecig: Nicotine-free e-liquids may only be tobacco-flavoured or unflavoured (Tobacco Act §32a), and the government has proposed banning them entirely. There is no channel for terpene-flavoured e-liquids.
